title: Strategic Account Director
description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Role

We’re looking for a Strategic Account Director that thrives in a highly autonomous environment. You’re product-minded, scrappy, and comfortable building your pipeline with some of the largest brands in the world. We have strong engineers on the team and the ability to aggressively support potential sales with customizations to close the deal. 



In this role, you will

 - Develop a strategy to break into and close key strategic logos for Decagon 

 - Develop deep, trusted relationships with key stakeholders at all levels of the customer organization (comfortable speaking to CX leaders, Product Leaders, and Operations Leaders) 

 - Understand the customer's business, challenges, and strategic priorities to uncover new opportunities for expansion 

 - Collaborate with internal teams (founders, deployment strategists, engineering, etc.) to deliver tailored solutions

 - Forecast and accurately report on pipeline and revenue 

 - Develop and execute account plans to execute strategic deals 

 - Provide feedback and insights to product and leadership teams to influence the company's roadmap

 - Maintain expert-level knowledge of the company's products, services, and industry trends

 - Expect moderate travel



Your background looks something like this

 - 7+ years of experience in strategic or enterprise sales

 - Proven track record of growing revenue and expanding business with large, complex accounts

 - Excellent communication, presentation, and negotiation skills

 - Strong business acumen and ability to speak the language of the C-suite

 - Consultative selling approach with a focus on value-based solutions

 - Ability to manage multiple stakeholders and cross-functional initiatives

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience



Even better if you have

 - Bonus points if you have previous experience selling AI or customer support/experience software



Benefits

We proudly offer the following benefits for our full-time employees:

 - Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life Insurance and Disability Benefits

 - Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K, pension)

 - Parental Leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Monthly stipend to support your wellness, lifestyle, and work-life balance

 - Daily lunches and snacks in the office to keep you at your best

 - Take what you need vacation policy (subject to local requirements; UK employees receive 25 days of statutory leave)

Decagon offers a competitive benefits package that varies by country and complements local statutory benefits. Details for this location will be provided during the recruitment process.

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
About us 
 Risk Ledger is developing a network of connected organisations, all working together to defend against cybersecurity attacks in the supply chain.
 Organisations rely on us to establish trust, through sharing their security maturity and visualising the risks posed by their supply chain ecosystem. And we’re already trusted by customers like British Airways, BAE Systems and the NHS.
 We are putting together an amazing and talented team from a diverse set of backgrounds and skillsets to drive us towards our vision. Risk Ledger is built on the respect we have for one another and our users, united by our shared values and mission.
 Every one of us is still learning: it’s how we grow as individuals. We’re curious. We’re ambitious. And we’re humble and honest. At Risk Ledger, we aim high to find the best solutions we can and always put our users first.
 This team: 
 You’ll join a cross‑functional Customer Success team that works hand‑in‑hand with Product, Marketing, Sales and the wider business to deliver real outcomes for our customers. We are collaborative partners, focussing on deeply understanding each customer’s context, goals and constraints.
 We continuously iterate on how we work, whether that is evolving our product, refining our playbooks, or improving our internal processes, so that we consistently deliver exceptional value to our users and to the business.
 This role: 
 You’ll join Risk Ledger as a Customer Success Manager, across mid‑market to enterprise accounts. Our team and customer base are growing quickly, and you’ll step into a role where you can design and improve our Customer Success approach, not just execute a standard set of tasks.
 You’ll have the opportunity to:
• Work closely with teams across the business on high‑impact initiatives, from onboarding and adoption programmes to advocacy and expansion plays.
• Help shape how we scale Customer Success, including in highly regulated environments.
• Take ownership of how we operationalise our strategy for your book of business, rather than simply managing a set of accounts.
 You will play a pivotal role in driving growth within our customer base, managing the entire customer lifecycle for your portfolio - from onboarding through to renewals and expansion. You’ll be accountable for ensuring your customers achieve meaningful outcomes with Risk Ledger, identifying and executing on growth opportunities, and ultimately maximising NRR across your portfolio.
 You’ll contribute directly to the development of our product by maintaining a tight feedback loop with our Product team. You’ll build strong, trusted relationships with your customers so you can deeply understand their needs and how they use our platform. You will be the voice of the customer internally, translating what you see and hear into actionable insight that shapes our strategy, roadmap and go‑to‑market.
 In the role you will: 
• Manage a portfolio of high‑touch customers, ensuring they successfully adopt Risk Ledger and achieve their business goals.
• Onboard new customers onto the Risk Ledger platform, including product implementation, training and change management with key stakeholders.
• Run regular business reviews with customers in order to collaborate with your customers to make sure they continuously remain engaged and achieve their goals
• Own the end‑to‑end renewal process for your customers, proactively understanding their sentiment and renewal intent to surface growth opportunities early and mitigate risk before it becomes urgent.
• Build strong relationships with senior stakeholders across multiple departments within your customers’ organisations, often in complex public‑sector structures.
• Be the voice of the customer inside Risk Ledger, collaborating closely with Product, Sales and Marketing to shape better solutions, inform our positioning, and drive growth across the wider business.
 You’ll have: 
• 3+ years of Customer Success experience, ideally in B2B SaaS or Cyber Security, working with mid‑market or enterprise accounts.
• Experience managing customers operating in similarly complex, regulated environments.
• A strong understanding of complex organisational structures and experience navigating multiple senior stakeholders with differing priorities.
• Excellent communication skills and a natural ability to build trust, ask the right questions and uncover where you can drive impact. You’re comfortable engaging key stakeholders, including in‑person meetings and workshops with senior decision‑makers.
• A highly collaborative mindset - you enjoy working with Product, Sales, Marketing and Support to deliver the best possible outcomes for customers and for the business.
• A genuine interest in technology and the curiosity to continuously learn new concepts, features and market trends - and translate them into value for your customers.
• A strong impact and results focus - you have a real sense of ownership, can prioritise across multiple complex customers, and understand the importance of measuring the success of your work against clear outcomes.
• High EQ is essential to succeed in this role. You’ll thrive in a low‑ego environment that values self‑awareness and two‑way feedback, and you’ll be on a continuous journey of personal and professional growth. You’ll be able to regulate your emotions and behaviour, stay resilient in a fast‑paced start‑up environment, and communicate and collaborate effectively with people from all walks of life.
 The perks: 
• 💰Competitive base salary
• 📈Generous EMI equity package
• 👌Private pension
• ✈️25 days annual leave + bank holidays
• 🏖Additional 30 days of unpaid leave per year to use as you wish
• 🎆Ad-hoc companywide time off - last year we gave everyone 'rest leave' in August and over the festive period
• 🏥Private healthcare with AXA Insurance - including enhanced mental wellbeing coverage
• 🏠Hybrid working policy, typically 2-3 days in the office
• 👶Enhanced family (parental) leave - gender-neutral polic

title: Account Manager
description:
Who we are:

Sardine is the leading agentic risk platform for fighting financial crime. Our integrated solution unifies data across risk teams to help organizations stop fraud in real time, prevent AI-driven attacks, and automate fraud and AML operations. Sardine’s platform is strengthened by one of the fastest-growing fraud consortiums in the market, spanning more than 6 billion profiled devices, 800 million consumers, and 3 million businesses worldwide. Leading companies including FIS, GoDaddy, Intuit, Edward Jones, ZoomInfo, and Checkout.com rely on Sardine to secure and grow trust in their products.



Our culture:

 - We hire talented, self-motivated individuals with extreme ownership and high growth orientation. 

 - We value performance and not hours worked. We believe you shouldn't have to miss your family dinner, your kid's school play, friends get-together, or doctor's appointments for the sake of adhering to an arbitrary work schedule.

 - We're a remote-first team spread across time zones, so no office to report to - work from wherever helps you do your best work. Just a couple of things to keep in mind: pay is based on where you're located, and you'll need to keep a home base in the country you're hired in. So while we love the "coffee shop today, mountains tomorrow" life, this isn't a passport-optional, work-from-anywhere-on-Earth kind of remote - think flexible within your country, not borderless.



Location:

 - Remote - Dubai



About the Role:

Sardine is rapidly acquiring new customers and executing on an ambitious roadmap. As a result, we're building a world-class customer success team to support our fraud, payments, and compliance-related products as we grow. As an Account Manager, you'll manage a handful of customers and act as their stakeholder within Sardine, helping maximize the value of our products and services. In addition, you will collaborate daily with Sardine teams to help customers meet their risk, fraud, compliance, and payment needs, including risk analytics, data science, integrations, and products.  



What you’ll be doing:

 - Be the primary point of contact for our customers, attending to day-to-day and 'big picture' problems and opportunities and helping maximize the customer's ROI in Sardine

 - Build a thorough understanding of our product, technology, and strategy and be able to message these succinctly to customers.

 - Translate complex product and technology problems into simple and actionable solutions. Be able to manage the solution process both internally and externally.

 - Speak knowledgeably and advise on best practices relating to fraud and compliance

 - Build, monitor, and communicate KPIs to clients.

 - Provide strategic analysis and critical thinking as we plan long-term expansion.

 - Work with Sardine's risk analytics teams to proactively solve new fraud typologies and actively communicate findings to customers.


What you’ll need:

 - 7+ years of experience in Account Management, Customer Success, Risk Management, or Solutions Architecture within B2B SaaS, with an understanding of how customers integrate API's

 - Domain experience in fraud, payments, compliance, fintech, or AML/KYC 

 - Experience working within the banking vertical is highly preferred

 - Strong presentation skills for both virtual and in-person meetings with various stakeholders

 - Previous customer-facing experience, preferably with a technical product

 - Exceptional project management skills and the ability to synthesize all inputs and balance the needs of multiple stakeholders

 - Proficiency in using business intelligence tools

 - Your analytical skills are second to none; you excel at number crunching and drawing insights

 - You're capable of translating complex strategies into actionable processes and outcomes

 - You're a natural at building relationships and collaborating with others

 - You constantly think about ways to improve processes

 - You love making customers more efficient as much as we do!



Benefits we offer:

 - Generous compensation in cash and equity

 - Early exercise for all options, including pre-vested

 - Work from anywhere: Remote-first Culture

 - Flexible paid time off and Year-end break

 - Health insurance, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents - US and Canada specific

 - 4% matching in 401k / RRSP - US and Canada specific

 - MacBook Pro delivered to your door

 - One-time stipend to set up a home office — desk, chair, screen, etc.

 - Monthly meal stipend

 - Monthly social meet-up stipend

 - Annual health and wellness stipend

 - Annual Learning stipend



Join a fast-growing company with world-class professionals from around the world. If you are seeking a meaningful career, you found the right place, and we would love to hear from you.



To learn more about how we process your personal information and your rights in regards to your personal information as an applicant and Sardine employee, please visit our Applicant and Worker Privacy Notice https://www.sardine.ai/applicant-and-worker-privacy-notice.

title: Account Manager
description:
About ComplyAdvantage 
 ComplyAdvantage is the financial industry’s leading source of AI-driven financial crime risk data and detection technology. Our mission is to neutralize the risk of money laundering, terrorist financing, corruption, and other financial crimes.
 More than 1,000 companies globally rely on us to navigate risk through the world’s only real-time database of people and companies. Backed by Goldman Sachs, Ontario Teachers’, Index Ventures, and Balderton Capital, we have raised over $100M to date. After growing our team by 40% last year, we are scaling from 500 to 600+ people to meet the massive market demand for RegTech innovation.
 The Role 
 We are looking for a commercially-minded Account Manager to protect and grow our footprint within the most innovative Fintechs, Banks, and Payment providers across EMEA.
 In this role, you aren't just a point of contact; you’re a strategic growth partner. You will own the commercial evolution of our most important relationships, identifying untapped 'white space' and navigating complex cross-sell and upsell cycles. You are responsible for ensuring our customers scale their partnership with ComplyAdvantage as their business grows, transforming existing accounts into high-value expansion engines
 What You Will Be Doing 
• Portfolio Ownership: Manage a diverse book of business with a dual focus on world-class retention (GRR) and aggressive expansion (NRR).
• Strategic Consulting: Build deep, multi-threaded relationships with senior decision-makers (C-Level, Compliance Leads, and Risk Officers) to understand their evolving business goals.
• Pipeline & Negotiation: Qualify expansion opportunities, lead commercial negotiations, and close upsell/cross-sell deals to overachieve against quarterly quotas.
• Executive Presence: Create urgency and demonstrate ROI, ensuring ComplyAdvantage remains a mission-critical component of your clients' tech stacks.
• Product Advocacy: Act as the "voice of the customer," feeding intelligence back to our Product and Strategy teams to shape our global roadmap.
• Internal Leadership: Contribute to our high-performance culture by sharing best practices and helping develop the next generation of AM talent.
 About You 
 You are a relationship-builder with a "closer" mindset. You enjoy the complexity of long-term account strategy and are motivated by seeing your customers succeed and grow.
 Your Experience 
• The Track Record: 4+ years of experience in Account Management or Customer Success (with a commercial quota), specifically within B2B SaaS.
• Industry Fluency: Experience in RegTech, Fintech, or Cloud solutions for Financial Services is highly preferred.
• Strategic Selling: You understand value-based selling and know how to map customer pain points to new product features.
• Methodology Driven: You use a structured approach to manage your accounts and pipeline (e.g., MEDDICC, Sandler, or Challenger).
 Your Traits 
• Commercial Acumen: You can spot an expansion opportunity from a mile away and know how to navigate a renewal negotiation effectively.
• Entrepreneurial Spirit: You thrive in fast-paced environments and are comfortable "building the playbook" as we scale.
• Collaborative: You enjoy working cross-functionally with Sales, Support, and Product teams to deliver a seamless customer experience.
• Ambitious: You are looking for a company where you can grow your career into leadership roles as the organization expands.
 Why Join Us? 
• Market Leader: Work with the industry-leading AI-driven risk data platform.
• Investment in You: We provide the technology and infrastructure you need to be successful. No "spreadsheet tracking," just high-velocity tools.
• Clear Career Path: With our 12-month expansion plan, we are actively looking for future leaders to help us scale the Account Management function.
 Benefits 
• Equity participation in our innovative mission to combat financial crime
• Unlimited Time Off Policy to promote work-life balance and well-being
• We embrace a hybrid approach that requires employees to be in the office for two days a week. We strongly believe that this approach fosters collaboration and enables the building of meaningful relationships
• Opportunities for collaboration and career development with smart, like-minded professionals
• Annual learning budget to support professional growth
• A home office budget to support working from home
• Enhanced parental leave and childcare benefits
• Life insurance and medical coverage through BUPA, including pre-existing conditions
• Pension contribution through The People's Pension
 About us: 
 Our mission is to empower every business to eliminate financial crime. 
 By harnessing AI, a unified platform, and an extensive partner ecosystem, we help customers turn compliance into a catalyst for growth, operational resilience, and enduring regulatory trust.
 More than 3,000 enterprises across 75 countries rely on our end-to-end platform and the world’s most comprehensive financial crime risk intelligence. With full-stack agentic automation, we help organizations automate up to 95% of KYC, AML, and sanctions reviews, cut onboarding times by 50%, reduce false positives by 70%, and handle 7x more work with the same staff.
 ComplyAdvantage is headquartered in London and has global hubs in New York, Lisbon, Singapore, and Cluj-Napoca. It is backed by Balderton Capital, Index Ventures, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, Goldman Sachs, and Andreessen Horowitz. Learn more about compliance re-engineered for the age of AI at complyadvantage.com .

title: Customer Success Manager
description:
The Company You’ll Join
 Carta is the connected platform and AI-native ecosystem for private capital. Built to replace fragmented tools with a single system of record, Carta brings together the software, services, and legal infrastructure that founders use to manage equity, fund managers use to run administration and reporting, and legal teams use to close transactions. Trusted by 55,000 companies and 1.8M+ equity holders in 160+ countries, and 10,000 funds and SPVs representing $250B+ in assets under management, Carta is transforming how private capital operates. Recognized by Fortune, Forbes, Fast Company, Inc. and Great Places to Work.
 For more information about our offices and culture, check out our Carta careers page .
 Strategic Customer Success Manager 
 Carta Law · Customer Success 
 About Carta Law 
 Carta Law is the world's largest AI-native legal services platform — rebuilding how legal work is structured, delivered and scaled. Combining deep legal expertise with proprietary AI infrastructure, we serve the world's leading venture-backed companies, founders and investors across every critical moment in a company's lifecycle: incorporation, fundraising, secondaries, governance and exit.
 We sit inside Carta — the operating system for private markets. Our captive client base spans more than 70,000 companies across every stage of growth, giving Carta Law a deal-flow advantage no traditional firm can replicate.
 We are not a traditional law firm. We are a technology company building the future of legal services — operating at the intersection of venture financing, software and AI, and scaling rapidly across the Americas, London and APAC. A dedicated team of R&D and product engineers, based across San Francisco, New York and London, works alongside our lawyers to build that future.
 The Problems You'll Solve 
 As a Strategic Customer Success Manager, you'll own our most important client relationships — managing high-value accounts with a high-touch model, building senior partnerships with the PE decision-makers who matter most, and driving the retention and expansion that gets Carta Law to its ambitious ARR goals.
 Our dedicated high-touch model has delivered exceptional YoY ARR growth on the accounts it covers. This role scales that model.
 Specifically, you'll:
• Manage a portfolio of high-value accounts with a high-touch coverage model — acting as the primary relationship point for senior PE stakeholders, GCs, and executive teams.
• Build deep, trusted relationships with PE decision-makers — not just day-to-day users — positioning Carta Law as a strategic partner rather than a vendor.
• Lead Quarterly Business Reviews with executive stakeholders, presenting ROI, strategic value, and roadmap alignment.
• Partner with Account Executives (AE) on upsell, cross-sell, and late-stage sales cycles — identifying whitespace across Contracts, Compliance, and Funds and converting commercial conversations into revenue.
• Serve as the escalation point for your accounts across legal delivery, finance, sales, and product — resolving complex issues with urgency and professionalism.
• Coordinate monthly data packs for your accounts, tracking NDR, retention rate, and expansion trends.
• Act as the voice of your clients internally — synthesising relationship intelligence, feedback, and usage signals to influence service design and product roadmap.
• Drive significant Net Dollar Retention across your portfolio.
 The Team You'll Work With 
 You'll be joining our Carta Law Customer Success (CS) team. We manage the full client lifecycle — from welcoming new clients through onboarding to building deep, lasting relationships with established fund managers and their legal teams.
 We sit at the intersection of legal delivery, commercial strategy, and operations. Day-to-day you'll partner closely with AEs, legal delivery, and product — serving as the connective tissue between Carta Law and our most strategic clients. You'll report to the Global Head of CS.
 About You 
 We're looking for a commercially sharp, relationship-driven senior professional who combines the strategic instincts of an account executive with the client-obsession of a great CS leader. You've managed complex, high-value relationships in fast-paced environments, and you know how to build trust at the executive level.
 Specifically, we're looking for:
• 5+ years of experience in Customer Success, Account Management, or a senior client-facing role within SaaS or professional/legal services. You've owned high-value relationships and have the commercial track record to show for it.
• Proven ability to manage senior stakeholder relationships . You're comfortable — and credible — in the room with GCs, CFOs, and PE decision-makers. You don't just manage accounts; you build partnerships.
• Strong commercial instincts . You spot cross-sell and upsell opportunities organically, and you know how to partner with sales to close them.
• Experience leading executive-level business reviews . You know how to frame value, present ROI, and hold a senior stakeholder's attention in a QBR.
• Full lifecycle ownership . You're comfortable managing clients from post-onboarding through to complex, mature relationships — adapting your approach at each stage.
• Outstanding verbal and written communication . You can break down complex legal, financial, or operational concepts for any audience, and you know how to tailor your message for the room.
• Data fluency . You track NDR, GDR, and expansion signals — and you use that data to drive conversations and decisions.
• High emotional intelligence . You read rooms well, navigate difficult conversations with professionalism and empathy, and maintain trust even when things get complicated.
• Prior experience in the legal industry or private markets is a significant advantage . Familiarity with venture capital, private equity, or fund operations gives you an immediate leg up in understanding our clients' world.

title: Customer Success Manager (London)
description:
Airtable helps organizations build the applications and workflows they need to run their most important business processes, without being constrained by off-the-shelf software. Its flexible platform combines a relational database, custom applications, automations, and AI, giving teams the building blocks to create solutions around the way they actually work. Just like Lego blocks, what our customers can build with Airtable is virtually limitless. That flexibility is why more than 500,000 organizations, including 80% of the Fortune 100, use Airtable to power critical work across their businesses.
 About the role 
 At Airtable, we are passionate about how our product democratizes software creation and empowers teams to build applications that connect their organization and drive outcomes, no code needed. As a Customer Success Manager, you will be the post-sales owner for a portfolio of enterprise customers, guiding them from onboarding through renewal as they adopt Airtable and our AI capabilities. You will help customers turn AI adoption and workflow innovation into measurable business outcomes, and you will partner closely with Account Executives so they can focus on growth.
 Customer Success at Airtable sits at the nexus of our Sales, Product and Marketing teams. We hire Customer Success Managers into one of two teams (Scaled and High Touch), depending on your experience and where our team needs you most. We will talk with you about which team is the best fit during the interview process.
 What you'll do
• Serve as the post-sales point of contact for your accounts, guiding customers to the right answer or the right Airtable team when you cannot resolve something yourself
• Drive onboarding excellence, working with customers on a mutual plan so their primary workflows launch within 90 days, with governance and best practices in place from the start
• Build joint success plans with customers focused on AI adoption, business outcomes and operational efficiency
• Lead Executive Business Reviews and data-driven value reviews that document ROI, surface risk and identify growth
• Develop champions across existing users so each account has multiple advocates who can sustain adoption
• Deliver enablement that accelerates adoption: Airtable 101, feature-specific sessions, AI and MCP workshops, and hands-on build sessions
• Guide governance conversations, including license deployment, long-term app strategy and stakeholder orchestration
• Run workflow consultations for new use cases and determine the right build path
• Monitor account health, adoption trends and risk signals, and flag risk early to your Account Executive and the Renewals team
• Qualify expansion opportunities and hand them to your Account Executive with context
• Maintain a current account record: use cases, success stories, ROI and a stakeholder map, refreshed quarterly
• Serve as the voice of the customer internally, translating usage and feedback into insights that shape our product and AI roadmap, and partner with Marketing and Product on customer stories
• Develop reusable frameworks, AI-enabled health insights and playbooks that scale customer impact across the enterprise segment
 Who you are
• You have 5+ years of experience in enterprise customer success, account management, solutions consulting or technical account management supporting B2B SaaS or workflow automation platforms
• You have a track record of delivering measurable results for customers through onboarding, adoption, retention and expansion
• You have owned relationships with multi-stakeholder enterprise accounts and are comfortable being the customer's primary contact
• You have technical fluency and can guide both business and technical audiences. You are comfortable discussing workflow automation, integrations and data, and you have a working understanding of AI and how customers apply it to real workflows

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation.  An overview of this role

You’ll partner with Ecosystem Sales, Partner Operations, Finance, Legal, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, and Enablement to launch and improve programs, recommend changes to incentives and policy, and connect program activity to pipeline, revenue, and customer outcomes. • Maintain program guides, eligibility rules, approval flows, and documentation, partnering with Legal and Finance so programs are compliant, auditable, and easy to understand.
• Create playbooks, launch materials, and training with Enablement and regional teams to drive adoption of new programs and commercial changes.

title: Programme Director EMEA
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


THE OPPORTUNITY

Snowflake works with the world's top 200 global companies. In this role you will build and lead Snowflake's programme delivery practice across EMEA, and stay close to the programmes that matter most to our largest customers: multi-year data, AI and modernisation transformations that change how those businesses run.

We are looking for a hands-on Programme Director. You have personally delivered complex, high-stakes programmes across several industries, and you still want to be close to the work. As a player-coach, you can build and lead a senior team and run a regional services business with commercial discipline. You also keep hands-on senior oversight of our most critical customer engagements. You are as credible in a programme steering committee or a customer boardroom as you are reviewing a delivery plan with your engineers. You'll report directly to the Regional Vice President, EMEA Services. Success means predictable delivery, healthy margin and customers who come back to us.

WHY THIS ROLE?

Lead with AI: Snowflake is a market leader in data and AI. You will shape how a regional delivery organisation uses AI and agentic tools to scope, deliver, assure and govern programmes faster and better.

Shape a new delivery model: We're moving services from time and materials to fixed fee fixed outcome mode as part of the new AI Engineering initiatives that are shaping the way our customers build their enterprise i.e we own the result for the customer.  You'll shape how delivery works in that model across EMEA.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Stay close to key engagements: Provide hands-on executive oversight of our most strategic and complex programmes. Step in personally where it matters, unblock escalations, and bring calm, decisive leadership to high-pressure situations.

Run the regional delivery business: Own EMEA delivery revenue, margin and forecast accuracy as we move from billable hours to fixed outcomes. Keep discipline on budgets and quarterly goals.

Build and lead a senior team: Hire, develop and retain a team of senior programme managers, delivery managers and architects. Set clear objectives, delegate well and hold the team accountable for results.

Champion AI-first delivery: Model and drive AI-forward ways of working across the team. Use Snowflake's AI and agentic capabilities, and wider AI tooling, to speed up scoping, migration, quality assurance, reporting and decision-making. Do this responsibly, with human oversight built in.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 
 An overview of this role 
 As Manager, SOX PMO - Business Process, you'll lead Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance for assigned business processes as part of GitLab's second line. This is advisory work, not repeatable testing: you'll deeply understand how processes work, evaluate risks as the business changes, and help control owners design and remediate controls that hold up to audit. Judgment matters more than procedure. You'll form well-supported conclusions, align with control owners and Internal Audit, and defend positions to external auditors. GitLab already uses AI extensively, and the next phase brings AI agents into our SOX processes. You'll help teams adopt them with confidence, finding creative ways to enable new ways of working while maintaining compliance. You'll also partner with the information technology (IT) SOX PMO on readiness for new systems and applications. This role reports to the Senior Director, SOX PMO, within the Chief Accounting Officer's organization.
 What You’ll Do 
• Lead SOX compliance for assigned business processes as the second-line subject matter expert, advising control owners who own and operate the controls. Deeply understand each process, its systems and data flows, and resolve open questions and assumptions early.
• Monitor risks from new and changing processes, products, and systems. Help control owners design, strengthen, or right-size controls, and contribute to the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping.
• Evaluate control deficiencies individually and in aggregate, identify root causes, and prepare well-supported severity assessments. Work with management to develop, implement, and monitor remediation plans.
• Prepare auditor-ready technical memos on sampling methodology, scoping, and control rationalization, using independent analysis and sound conclusions. Prepare reports and presentations on SOX compliance status for leadership.
• Lead business walkthroughs and stakeholder meetings, and coordinate with Internal Audit and external auditors throughout the audit. Anticipate questions, support positions with data and judgment, and escalate risks and auditor comments promptly with a recommended path forward.
• Advise on controls for AI-enabled processes and processes that use AI agents. Find opportunities to automate SOX work using AI tools, and validate their output.
• Partner with the IT SOX PMO to assess new systems and controls, including application controls and key reports.
• Develop and maintain accurate process narratives, flowcharts, and risk and control matrices as processes change. Collaborate with Finance, Operations, Legal, Human Resources, Sales, Engineering, and IT leaders to help them design and maintain effective business controls.
 What You’ll Bring 
• Hands-on SOX and internal controls experience in control design, remediation, and deficiency evaluation, beyond testing alone. Experience in the software or technology industry is required; SOX PMO, Big Four risk advisory, or assurance experience is a strong plus.
• A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; an active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) credential (strongly preferred) or Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) credential.
• A strong understanding of SOX requirements and internal control frameworks, such as the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework.
• Professional judgment and skepticism: verifying facts against source documents, testing the reasonableness of data and conclusions, and recognizing missing information.
• A track record of independently solving ambiguous, novel problems, from defining an approach through overcoming obstacles and driving resolution. Curiosity to understand how processes actually work and keep learning as the business changes.
• Clear written and verbal communication, including concise, accurate, auditor-ready memos and actionable recommendations. Confidence partnering with senior stakeholders and external auditors, including working through pushback.
• A practical, innovative approach to helping the business adopt new technologies, products, and ways of working while maintaining compliance. Experience using AI tools to improve efficiency and validating their output.
• Experience with usage-based billing or AuditBoard is a plus.

 The SOX PMO is part of the Chief Accounting Officer's organization. In this role, you'll advise business control owners and partner with the IT SOX PMO, Internal Audit, and external auditors to keep GitLab compliant as processes, systems, and AI use evolve. title: Staff Strategic Operations Program Manager - GTM
location: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States
description:
Until November 18, 1883, American railroads ran on dozens of local times. Noon in Chicago was 12:31 in Pittsburgh, and every railroad kept its own clock, so schedules collided and connections failed. That day the railroads agreed on four time zones, and clocks across the country stopped and restarted on a shared standard. Nothing about the trains changed. What changed was that everyone could finally plan against the same clock.
 That is the job of the Staff Strategic Operations Program Manager for Go-to-Market (“GTM”) at Mercury.
 Mercury builds the financial stack for ambitious businesses: banking*, cards, payments, credit, and the financial workflows that run on top of them. Our go-to-market organization spans Revenue, Marketing, Growth Product, and GTM Data, more than 200 people who acquire customers and help them use more of Mercury. 
 To do that, the four teams are building a shared GTM Engine: one view of the customer, every touchpoint logged, attribution everyone trusts, and Campaigns that share targeting and rules across channels. This role owns the whole program end to end. You would be that person, sitting on Mercury’s Strategic Operations team and embedded with GTM leadership.
 *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.
 What you’ll do: 
 Own the program 
• Build and run the integrated plan for the GTM Engine across Growth Product, Growth Marketing, Revenue, and GTM Data: milestones, dependencies, critical path, and the handoffs between teams that no single team owns.
• Keep a living RAID log and decision log with clear owners. When a data signal slips and a campaign depends on it, you know first and arrive with options.
 Drive decisions 
• Drive decisions through ambiguity: clarify ownership, force tradeoffs into the open, and use productive conflict to get to the right answer
• Prepare GTM Review so leaders spend their time deciding rather than reconstructing status. 
 Build the operating system 
• Design the planning cycles, reviews, and launch-readiness checks that let four teams work the same customer at the same time.
• Make the engine legible: dashboards, written updates, and a single source of truth that a marketer, a sales leader, and a data scientist can all read.
• Build automation and agentic flows to run programs with efficiency and high quality
 What we’re looking for: 
• 7+ years running cross-functional programs, ideally in B2B SaaS or fintech. 
• GTM systems fluency. You have worked inside a CRM, lifecycle, CDP, or attribution stack (Salesforce, Customer.io, Segment, or equivalents) closely enough to know what is hard about getting a new signal into a rep’s or a marketer’s workflow. 
• Structured thinking. You take disparate inputs (four leaders, three functions, dozens of docs) and turn them into one picture of what is happening and what needs deciding.
• Strong structured communication
• Bias to action. You pick up the unowned next step, you do not let ambiguity sit, and you go talk to whoever has the answer.
• Low ego. This is a behind-the-scenes role.
• AI fluency. You have already automated some of your own work and can show the before and after.
 Mercury values diversity & belonging and is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. All individuals seeking employment at Mercury are considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, veteran status, gender identity, sexual orientation, or any other legally protected characteristic. If you need assistance, or an accommodation, please let your recruiter know once you are contacted about a role.

 Equal Opportunity

title: Programme Manager, Commercial Incentives
description:
Our Global Structure 
Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.
 About The Role 
 As Programme Manager, Commercial Incentives, you will be responsible for managing Deliveroo’s approach to commercial incentives. You will work with our local markets to define commercial teams’ KPIs and incentive plans that align with Deliveroo’s business and financial objectives. You will support local market leadership, ensuring schemes are understood and embedded in their day to day operations. You will be responsible for managing the schemes on an ongoing basis, including the execution of schemes and performance tracking. 
 About the Team
 You will be part of the wider Commercial Operations team who enable our frontline commercial teams through commercial insight, learning and development, and change management in all markets. 
 What you’ll be responsible for 
 Owning the ongoing management of incentive schemes 
• Own the ongoing management and administration of incentive schemes. Work to design and implement workflows and tooling to streamline the management of incentives.
• Lead the monthly and quarterly calculation of incentive plans (in collaboration with local leadership), managing exceptions, accuracy checks, and ensuring data quality and consistency across all schemes.
• Build and document scalable processes to support local leaders with target setting.
• Own commercial performance reporting to identify trends, diagnose issues, and highlight opportunities to improve incentive design.
• Partner with the Product team to migrate incentive management from spreadsheets to new, engaging, and user-friendly systems.
 Support the design of efficient and effective commercial incentive schemes 
• Act as a subject matter expert in the design of commercial incentive schemes, supporting the Commercial Incentives Manager in creating a globally centralised framework.
• Partner with local commercial leaders as they define their incentive schemes, helping them assess trade-offs between different design options.
• Conduct initial impact assessments of proposed schemes under various scenarios (e.g. total cost, payout distribution, and behavioural implications).
• Support local commercial leaders to prepare their “go-to-market” for new incentive schemes such that they are clear and engaging for the incentive participants
 Key Competencies 
• Attention to Detail: Demonstrates exceptional attention to detail, ensuring calculations are accurate so that Commercial teams are paid correctly and on time.
• Data Analytics: Skilled in analysing and interpreting data using BI tools (e.g. Looker, Tableau) and Microsoft Excel to derive insights and support decision-making.
• Project Management: Proven ability to manage and progress multiple complex projects in parallel, coordinating across stakeholders, markets and functions.
• Communication & Influence: Listens actively. Simplifies complex ideas and communicates clearly. Collaborates effectively across a wide range of teams and senior stakeholder groups. 
• Problem-solving & Strategic Thinking: Able to understand complex business context quickly, articulate tradeoffs, and recommend solutions. Understands the strategic implications of their work, is able to anticipate risks and suggest ways to mitigate.
• Team Development and Community-Building : Is a team player who readily collaborates cross-functionally and can resolve areas of misalignment or conflict between teams. Finds opportunities to build a sense of community and coach more junior team members.
 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 
At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.

 The Senior Client Manager builds trusted, long-term relationships with corporate clients, developing a deep understanding of their businesses, brands, organizational priorities and challenges. Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

title: Associate Director - Client Success
description:
About us

ClearBank was built on the belief that banking infrastructure would no longer slow down progress. Instead, it’s the catalyst that unlocks the potential to innovate. That’s why our clients — financial institutions from fintech’s and crypto platforms, to banks and credit unions — use our API to power their banking infrastructure.

But we wouldn’t be ClearBank without our people. They’re what powers our innovative technology and the reason we love what we do every day. We’re a group of spirited people who are never afraid to challenge the norm – becoming stronger, more energised, and that much better when we’re together.

It’s our belief in fairness, autonomy and choice that means our people are empowered with the tools to learn, grow, and contribute to ours and our clients’ success.

Interested in joining us? Read on or visit our website for more information.

About you

As an Associate Director in the Client Success team, play a crucial role in maintaining and growing a portfolio of some of our largest and most strategic clients. Reporting to Senior Director – Client Success, you’ll be a part of a fast-growing business that is challenging the market and doing things differently.

You'll take ownership of a portfolio of ClearBank's key Enterprise grade clients, committing to their success, and relentlessly work to remove barriers to adoption, both within their organisation and cross-functionally within ClearBank. You will be responsible for ensuring the success of our clients and driving revenue growth.

And you’ll be joining one of the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK, according to Deloitte Fast 50. You will be:

 - Managing and maintaining a portfolio of strategic Enterprise client relationships, ensuring their satisfaction and success with ClearBank's services.

 - Delivering a high-quality and positive client experience, building strong relationships and trust with your clients, working towards their strategic goals.

 - Achieving clear client retention and revenue growth goals by proactively identifying and capitalising on upselling and cross-selling opportunities, working towards an annual quota.

 - Collaborating closely with internal stakeholders, including Sales, Finance, Financial Crime, Legal, Marketing, and Customer Operations teams.

 - Representing and being an advocate for your clients within ClearBank, ensuring their needs and requirements are understood and addressed.

 - Conducting regular and quality engagement with your clients, maintaining a strong presence and providing ongoing support.

 - Managing a regular cadence of communication and conduct business reviews with clients



What we are looking for

 - Significant previous experience in commercial/sales focused relationship management roles.

 - Proven track record of achieving client retention and revenue growth targets through upselling and cross-selling to large, enterprise-grade existing clients.

 - Knowledge of the banking industry and financial products is required.

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills, able to effectively engage with clients and internal stakeholders at all levels, including c-suite executives.

 - Excellent problem-solving skills, able to identify and overcome barriers to adoption and drive client success.

 - Ability to collaborate and work effectively across multiple teams, fostering a culture of teamwork and shared goals.

 - Strong organisational skills, able to manage multiple client relationships and prioritise tasks effectively.

 - Inquisitive and comfortable asking questions about clients' business goals, ideal state, and pain points.

 - Ability to analyse multiple problems, develop and drive solutions.

 - Confidence in working in the unknown, taking initiative, and designing processes when they don't yet exist.

 - Passion for technology and being part of a fast-growing company.

 - Good organisational skills and high attention to detail.

 - Proactive and resourceful, able to take ownership and drive results.

A little bit more about us! 



ClearBank is Where You Can belong: 

At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of: 

 - 42% of our senior management roles are held by women 

 - Our enhanced family leave policies

 - Launching our partnership with Code First Girls 

 - Increasing awareness of neurodiversity in the workplace through our partnership with the Inclusive Group 



Our hiring process and what you can expect:

Application: a member of our talent acquisition team will review your application against the key requirements for the role and let you know within two weeks whether you’re moving forward to the next stage; 

Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too); 

First Interview: You’ll spend one hour with a member of our hiring team focusing on your skills, competencies and your ways of working at the same time we’ll give you time to ask more questions about the role, the team and learn more about the ClearBank culture. This will be via Teams.  

Second Interview: This will be a competency-based interview with one or more members of our team.

Final Stage: You will have a final meeting with the Head of Department. This will be around 45-60 minutes.

description:

FARFETCH exists for the love of fashion. Our mission is to be the global platform for luxury fashion, connecting creators, curators and consumers.

We're a positive platform for good, bringing together an incredible creative community made up by our people, our partners and our customers. This community is at the heart of our business success. We welcome differences, empower individuality and celebrate diverse skills and perspectives, creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We are FARFETCH for All.

LEGAL, ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE

Working in close partnership, the Legal and Ethics & Compliance (E&C) teams operate as a strategic business area helping us navigate the complexities of a global business. The Legal team acts as guardians of our legal integrity, providing expert advice to protect our interests and manage risks.  Alongside them, the E&C team drives our commitment to doing business the right way by developing robust compliance frameworks, monitoring regulatory adherence, and fostering a strong culture of ethical conduct.

LONDON

Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events.

THE ROLE

The Compliance team is focused on ensuring regulatory compliance as well as compliance with our Code of Conduct and Company Policies.

As a Compliance Program Manager, you will serve as a subject matter expert responsible for the end-to-end management of critical compliance pillars... Your expertise will ensure that our global operations remain ethical, compliant with international and external regulations.

Please note: This is a 12m FTC role. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 1. Overall Program Management

 - Lead the periodic review, enhancement, and localized rollout of global compliance policies and procedures to ensure alignment with evolving business needs and regulatory landscapes.

 - Monitor and manage the compliance group email to ensure continuous and seamless communication.

 - Review and provide operational guidance on generic compliance advice requests from across the business.

 - Centrally manage compliance activities and maintain program trackers, utilizing this data to prepare and deliver periodic compliance reports for senior leadership.

 2. Training and Awareness

 - Raise awareness of Ethics & Compliance policies and standards amongst existing employees and lead the onboarding processes for new employees.

 - Manage the global Training & Awareness (T&A) calendar, ensuring all mandatory compliance training modules and communications are appropriately and timely developed and implemented across the organization.

 3. Ethics & Policy Governance

 - Raise awareness of Ethics & Compliance policies and standards, including the Code of Conduct, Conflicts of Interest, Gift & Entertainment policies etc. amongst existing employees and lead the onboarding processes for new employees. 

 - Ensure relevant compliance policies are updated/refreshed from time to time. Deploy suitable training for at-risk populations on compliance policies and requirements.

 - Implement a compliance declaration process and tools/forms for new joiners and existing employees. Actively review and manage these declarations in line with company policies.

 4. Regulatory and Product Compliance

 - Develop and enforce a robust compliance framework to ensure relevant controls are in place to comply with regional safety, labelling, and certification standards (e.g., CE, UKCA, or INFORM Act) across a multi-jurisdictional marketplace.

 - Collaborate with business and legal teams to define restricted-item policies and automated gatekeeping/blocking mechanisms for high-risk product groups.

 5. Other Compliance Initiatives

 - Support the wider compliance team with other compliance initiatives across related compliance areas from time to time. 

 - Provide timely and relevant information and feedback to the wider Compliance team and respective business functions to plug process gaps or internal control defects.

WHO YOU ARE:

 - Bachelor’s degree in a related field with robust experience managing corporate ethics and compliance programs. 

 - Strong project management and analytical skills, with a proven track record of successfully overseeing complex, cross-functional initiatives and operationalizing compliance frameworks.

 - Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to translate complex regulatory requirements into practical, easily understood guidance for the business.

 - Highly organized, proactive, and capable of working autonomously to drive program deliverables while maintaining excellent attention to detail.

 - Demonstrated experience in designing, implementing, and monitoring compliance policies, conflict of interest programs, and global training rollouts.

REWARDS & BENEFITS:

 - Employee Pension Scheme 

 - Flexible Benefits Program 

 - Health Insurance & Critical Illness cover 

 - Flexible work environment- Hybrid Model (3 days a week from the office, 2 days from home)

title: Transformation Advisory Lead, Strategy & Economics, EMEA
description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.




ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey is building a legal transformation practice for the AI era. Our Transformation Office brings together highly experienced consultants and practitioners to help law firms and legal departments turn AI from a tool their teams use into value their business can see.

Harvey’s experts help leaders decide what to change, and how to change it, as they adopt and embed new ways of working: how legal work is organized and governed, how it’s priced by firms and valued by in-house teams and how their people build new capability. The Transformation Office then works alongside their teams to make it happen. Our advice draws on what we see across Harvey's customers in more than 50 countries and on where the technology is heading. Our client work shapes Harvey's product, and the product shapes our advice. Both improve together.

Law firms and legal departments are making decisions now that will shape how they compete for the next decade: which work to prioritize, how to price and value it, how to staff it and how to organize around AI. As Transformation Advisory Lead for Strategy & Economics, you help their leaders make those decisions well. You have made them yourself, inside a firm or a legal department, and advised others through them, so managing partners, general counsel and CFOs treat you as a peer.

You will be one of the first senior specialists in Harvey's Transformation Office. You will help build our strategy and economics offering, bring that expertise to client engagements run by our Engagement Managers and join our Practice Directors when a customer has a specific need in strategy and economics. What you learn will shape how Harvey advises the market and what we build next.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Advise on strategy. Help leaders decide where AI changes their competitive position: which practices/domains, clients and types of work to prioritize, and where to invest.

 - Advise on pricing and value. Help firms and legal departments measure the impact of AI on the cost, speed and value of their work. For firms, that means working through how fee structures and value models need to change; for legal departments, it means showing the value their work creates for the business.

 - Advise on operating models. Help customers redesign how legal work is organized, supported and staffed, including team structures and the roles AI creates or changes.

 - Help leaders make the case for change. Work with managing partners, general counsel and finance leaders to build the case they take to their partnership, board, internal stakeholders or executive team.

 - Build the offering. Create the diagnostics, frameworks and leadership readouts the Transformation Office uses to deliver strategy and economics engagements, and turn each engagement into material the wider team can use.

 - Bring your expertise to early conversations. Join Practice Directors and account teams when a customer has a specific need in strategy and economics.



WHAT YOU HAVE

 - 10+ years of experience, including significant time shaping strategy, pricing or operating decisions: for example in a law firm's strategy, pricing or practice management team, in legal operations, external counsel or law firm management, or as chief of staff to a general counsel. Experience in a legal-sector consulting practice is a strong plus.

 - Deep fluency in legal economics. For law firms: leverage, practice-group and matter profitability, pricing and fee structures. For legal departments: cost-center dynamics, outside-counsel spend and how the value of legal work is measured.

 - A track record of advising senior legal leaders through high-stakes decisions, with the presence to hold a room that includes finance.

 - A clear point of view on how AI will change the business of law, grounded in how the economics actually move.

 - Evidence that you have built frameworks or methods that others adopted and kept using.

 - The judgment to discuss efficiency in a way that builds support for change rather than fear about displacement.

 - Energy for building something new while the playbook is still being written.

title: EMEA Regulatory Lead - Drones
description:
Our Global Structure 
Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.
 About the Team 
 We're building drone delivery for the long term. We already operate certified drone programmes in the US, and we’re now taking that to Europe and the Middle East, working closely with Deliveroo’s operations, policy and go-to-market teams. If you want to help decide how autonomous aviation gets approved and scaled in new markets, we want to talk to you.
 About the Role 
 As the EMEA Regulatory Lead, you will be the face of drone delivery to aviation regulators in the UK, the EU and the Middle East. Regulation here is built on relationships and trust as much as paperwork, and you’ll be the person who builds both. You’ll set the regulatory strategy, steer a specialist consultant team through permits and operational approvals, and shape how a new category of aircraft operation is approved in major markets.
 This is a new role. Consultants are already working on approvals to fly. You’ll take over those relationships and that workstream, and build the in-region regulatory function from the ground up. You’ll report to DoorDash's Drones Regulatory and Policy Lead in the US, and work alongside the operations team based at Deliveroo’s London office.
 What You’ll Do Day to Day 
 Own the Regulator Relationships: 
• Be the primary point of contact for the UK CAA, the Irish Aviation Authority, EASA and national authorities, and other regulators.
• Meet regulators directly to explain our concept of operations, technology and safety case, and build the trust needed to unlock new markets and capabilities.
• Advocate for policy changes that address authorities’ concerns while enabling scalable, risk-proportionate deployment beyond trials and demonstrations.
 Drive Approvals: 
• Own SORA-style application packages end to end, pulling technical, safety and operational input from engineering, product, safety and operations into complete submissions, and driving them through approval.
• Manage the consultants who do the groundwork on permits and operational approvals, including scope, timelines and quality.
• Help sequence target markets and capabilities based on regulatory feasibility, timeline and risk, so expansion decisions rest on regulatory reality. 
• Support the permit push once the launch aircraft is confirmed.
 Shape Strategy and Policy: 
• Partner with DoorDash leadership on international deployment strategy for the EU, UK and Middle East.
• Align with our US-based UAS Regulatory & Policy Lead to share playbooks and precedents and keep our position consistent on cross-border issues such as standards and cross-recognition of approvals.
• Act as the link between DoorDash Air and Deliveroo’s policy and go-to-market teams, so aviation positions fit with Deliveroo’s wider European government affairs work.
• Track legislative, regulatory and industry developments in UAS, U-Space and UTM, and turn them into clear recommendations for leadership.
 Represent Us Externally: 
• Speak for the company at European and Middle Eastern conferences and industry forums. Travel is occasional, mainly regional events and regulator meetings.
• Engage with UAS and UTM advocacy and standards bodies (for example JARUS) so our operational and technical needs are reflected in emerging frameworks.
 Build the Function: 
• Set up the processes, governance and relationships that let us run regulatory work across the region, and shape what the team looks like as we grow.
 What We’re Looking For 
• A traditional aviation background, either as a pilot or aviator or as a regulator, with a solid understanding of the drone and unmanned aircraft industry and its key issues.
• 10+ years in aviation regulatory affairs, government affairs or public policy, with current depth in UAS regulation. This is a mid-senior role that needs subject-matter expertise from day one.
• Working command of JARUS SORA and of the national and European authority processes (UK CAA, IAA, EASA) for UAS and BVLOS approvals.
• Detailed knowledge of how the airspace system works, including how unmanned aircraft are kept clear of crewed and other unmanned aircraft.
• Experience assembling and submitting SORA-style packages, or assessing them from the regulator side.
• The gravitas and communication skills to represent a company to regulators and argue its case, and to turn complex regulatory issues into clear decisions for senior leaders.
• Basic project management skills, with experience managing consultants or external partners.
• Based in, or willing to relocate to, London or elsewhere in Europe.
• Fluent English.
 Bonus Qualifications 
• Experience as a regulator, or an existing network of regulator relationships across the UK, EU and Middle East.
• Experience in the Middle East or familiarity with the UAE regulatory landscape.
• A second European or regional language (for example French, German or Arabic).
• Experience representing an organisation in UAS or UTM standards bodies and industry conferences.
• Experience in commercial drone delivery or other industry operations.

At Funding Circle, we have the restless energy of a fintech start-up with the stability of a public company. It’s a unique mix that gives Circlers the autonomy to take ownership and the scale to make an impact that truly counts.



We’re a high-performing team that chooses to lift each other up. We challenge, we champion, and we have each other’s backs -  because we know that when we stand together, we move faster and build better.



The impact is real: Last year alone, the businesses on our platform generated £7.2bn for the UK economy 📈 Come and join a mission that matters!

[Read our Impact Report https://www.fundingcircle.com/uk/impact] | [See our Trustpilot https://uk.trustpilot.com/review/fundingcircle.com]




THE ROLE ⚡

📍 London (Hybrid) | 🤝 3 days in the office | 💰 Competitive Salary + Benefits



This role assists customers who require additional care and support due to their health, financial and personal circumstances. You will manage them through the collections process, and recovery process, while leading with clear and compassionate communication.



 - Manage a portfolio of diverse vulnerable customers, guiding them through the debt recovery process with empathy, clarity, and professionalism.

 - Set up affordable payment plans and clearly break down the details of outstanding balances and payments into plain, accessible language for customers.

 - Effectively signpost customers to relevant charities, free legal advice services, and external support organisations.

 - Engage effectively with customers via verbal and written correspondence.

 - Navigate difficult and emotionally charged conversations regarding personal circumstances, including those involving mental health and, at times, suicidal ideation, with compassion and resilience.

 - Apply critical thinking to accounts, by balancing commercial requirements with the needs of the vulnerable customer.
   
   

Hear from our some of our Vulnerable Customer Account Managers https://www.youtube.com/watch?list=PLHFJpP8HNhB4&v=L0sa1k27BAw about what it's like to be part of our Vulnerable Customer Team!




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR 🌱



We value deep expertise, but a growth mindset and good energy are what really make our team click. We’re a group that chooses to lift each other up and think smart every day.



 - Proven experience handling vulnerable customers impacted by mental health, physical health and life events.

 - Practical experience managing customers through the debt recovery process.

 - Strong ability to understand various financial product types such as term loans, credit cards.

 - Deep empathy balanced with strong attention to detail, professionalism, and personal resilience during sensitive customer interactions.

 - Excellent written communication skills, with the ability to draft tailored emails, bespoke to the customers needs.

 - Thrives in a deadline-driven environment, maintaining compliance and high-quality standards under pressure.

 - Comfortable speaking with customers who may be experiencing severe distress, depression, or suicidal thoughts. Please consider this aspect carefully before applying if it is triggering for you.

 - Able to proactively identify ways to use Generative AI to streamline your daily tasks and improve your personal productivity

 - Confident using approved AI tools safely and effectively to enhance your output and find a better way of working

We’re building a place where everyone truly feels they belong. Even if your past experience doesn't align perfectly with every requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.




WHY JOIN US? 💜

We back you to build an incredible career and by joining us, you'll be part of one of The Sunday Times Best Companies to Work For 2026! As a flexible-first employer, we use a "best of both" approach. We’ll see you in our London office to collaborate – with barista coffee and subsidised Just Eat lunches on us!

Our Circler Proposition focuses on five areas:

 - Flexibility: We provide a benefit allowance you can tailor to your own life and family.

 - Health: This includes private medical and dental, health assessments, and access to a digital GP.

 - Wealth: We offer life assurance, share schemes, and financial coaching.

 - Development: You get a dedicated annual learning allowance to help you level up.

 - Lifestyle: We have electric car and cycle-to-work schemes, plus season ticket loans.

We also have award-winning parental leave policies. We're here to support you through the big life moments, from fertility treatments to new additions to the family.

We're a positive platform for good, bringing together an incredible creative community made up by our people, our partners and our customers. This community is at the heart of our business success. We welcome differences, empower individuality and celebrate diverse skills and perspectives, creating an inclusive environment for everyone. We are FARFETCH for All.

LEGAL, ETHICS AND COMPLIANCE

Working in close partnership, the Legal and Ethics & Compliance (E&C) teams operate as a strategic business area helping us navigate the complexities of a global business. The Legal team acts as guardians of our legal integrity, providing expert advice to protect our interests and manage risks.  Alongside them, the E&C team drives our commitment to doing business the right way by developing robust compliance frameworks, monitoring regulatory adherence, and fostering a strong culture of ethical conduct.

LONDON

Our London office is located in Old Street, London’s tech hub, and is home to a wide range of teams. Our open space is ideal for collaborative work and sharing ideas. We also have a large outdoor terrace, which is the perfect spot to have a team lunch or host events.

THE ROLE

The Principal, Financial Crime and Regulatory Compliance is a senior role responsible for building, scaling, and overseeing global AML and Sanctions compliance programs that protect the company from regulatory, financial, and reputational risk.

WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 - Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Program
   
   - Design and lead AML frameworks across multiple jurisdictions, including Due Diligence, and Suspicious Transaction Reporting.
   
   - Establish consistent governance standards, documentation requirements, and operational controls to ensure regulatory alignment across markets.
   
   - Identify emerging AML risk typologies and direct the development of analytic methods, and escalation criteria.
   
   - Conduct comprehensive enterprise-wide AML risk assessments and implement robust remediation plans to address identified vulnerabilities.
   
   - Serve as the principal liaison for internal audits, external regulatory examinations, and law enforcement inquiries related to money laundering.
   
   Transaction Monitoring, Fraud & Ecosystem Defense
   
   - Design and manage Transaction Monitoring frameworks to identify suspicious activities and financial crime typologies across the global platform.
   
   - Extend Transaction Monitoring capabilities to function as a holistic defense mechanism, integrating preventative controls over fraud, Trust and Safety, and payment anomalies.
   
   - Support the design and operation of monitoring mechanisms for fraud, seller abuse, or related risk indicators, coordinating with internal functions as needed.
   
   - Partner with engineering and data teams to deploy advanced monitoring rules and real-time detection solutions to protect the platform's ecosystem.
   
   Sanctions Compliance Management
   
   - Lead global sanctions screening for new and existing partners/customers and ensure compliance with U.S., U.K., E.U., and other applicable sanctions regimes.
   
   - Oversee sanctions system configuration, alert review procedures, and escalation protocols to maintain screening accuracy and defensibility.
   
   - Implement and manage comprehensive e-commerce sanctions controls beyond entity screening, including IP geolocation blocking, restricted delivery address logic, and cross-border shipping restrictions for high-risk regions.
   
   - Provide guidance to business teams on sanctions implications for customers, products, and market expansion.
   
   - Monitor real-time geopolitical developments and proactively update internal sanctions policies to mitigate emerging jurisdictional risks.
   
   - Establish ongoing testing and calibration routines for screening tools to minimize false positives and optimize tools.

   - Continuously assess evolving legal and regulatory requirements across multiple global jurisdictions to ensure the compliance framework remains robust and current.
   
   - Provide strategic advice, interpretation, and counsel to business units and executive leadership on applicable AML, Sanctions, and Financial Crime obligations.
   
   - Design, implement, and oversee comprehensive compliance training and awareness programs tailored to relevant teams and departments, fostering a proactive culture of risk management.
